svg.text: DIKW: data becomes wisdom at the bedside

g.text: WISDOM
"hold the dose"
nurse decides!
KNOWLEDGE — protocol says
"K+ 6.1 + peaked T = emergency"
INFORMATION — lab + ECG linked
"this result + this tracing = pattern"
DATA — raw facts typed in
"K+ 6.1" · "T-wave peaked" · "BP 90/60"
READ UP: nurses feed data, systems build information, protocols add knowledge —
but only the NURSE turns it into wisdom ("call the doctor NOW, hold the drug"). Garbage
typed in = garbage wisdom out: your keystrokes ARE patient safety.
INFORMATICS = people + data + technology improving care (IMIA/ANA). Not "IT for nurses" —
nursing judgment expressed through digital tools. Every chart entry, alert answer and
DHIMS2 figure is informatics in action.
ROLES LADDER: bedside nurse (accurate data!) → super-user (ward trainer) → analyst (builds
reports) → informaticist (designs systems) → CNIO (leads strategy). Exams ask the LADDER
order + the TIGER competencies: basic computer skills, information literacy, information
management. Every nurse needs rung 1–2; specialists climb higher.
WISDOM TEST: "system says discharge, gut says deteriorating?" — wisdom overrides: reassess,
escalate, document WHY. Computers suggest; nurses decide; patients live with it.
MANTRA: "right data, right person, right time — decided by the right nurse."
